title: 189. Australian Prime Ministers: Bob Hawke - Scott Morrison (Part 3)

sentences.en: I like him personally, but I think he's as mad as a cut snake.
sentences.zh: 我个人挺喜欢他，但我觉得他疯得像条被砍了一刀的蛇。

sentences.en: What's the bugger going to say next?
sentences.zh: 这家伙接下来又要说什么？

sentences.en: That's a random Australian talking about my co-presenter, Tom Holland, quoting Bob Hawke, Prime Minister of Australia,
sentences.zh: 那是一位澳大利亚路人谈论我的联合主持人汤姆·霍兰德时说的话，他引用了澳大利亚前总理鲍勃·霍克的话，

sentences.en: talking about another Prime Minister of Australia many years later, Tony Abbott.
sentences.zh: 而霍克当时谈论的是多年后的另一位澳大利亚总理托尼·阿博特。

sentences.en: So Australians, Tom, if you've ever watched debates from the Australian legislature, they have a splendid way with words.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，如果你看过澳大利亚立法机构的辩论，你会发现澳大利亚人在用词上确实有一套。

sentences.en: I haven't really, but I have watched, obviously, Ashes series.
sentences.zh: 我没怎么看过，但我显然看过“骨灰杯”板球系列赛。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: So I've seen how Australians behave to visiting English cricketers.
sentences.zh: 所以我见过澳大利亚人是怎么对待来访的英格兰板球运动员的。

sentences.en: Political sledging.
sentences.zh: 政治上的“雪橇”战术（垃圾话）。

sentences.en: They're absolutely brilliant at political sledging.
sentences.zh: 他们在政治垃圾话方面简直是天才。

sentences.en: Yeah, sledging is the great Australian art.
sentences.zh: 没错，垃圾话是伟大的澳大利亚艺术。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Mental disintegration.
sentences.zh: 精神摧毁。

sentences.en: So for our overseas listeners who don't know what sledging is, sledging is basically just abuse.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些不知道什么是“雪橇”战术的海外听众，这基本上就是辱骂。

sentences.en: Abuse.
sentences.zh: 辱骂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you were quoting Bob Hawke.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才引用的是鲍勃·霍克。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's where we got to.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才聊到这儿了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we've been going through Australia's wartime and post-war Prime Ministers.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在梳理澳大利亚战时及战后的总理们。

sentences.en: We were planning to do it in one episode.
sentences.zh: 我们本来打算用一集讲完。

sentences.en: Then we were planning to do it in two episodes.
sentences.zh: 后来打算用两集。

sentences.en: But there are just so many Australian Prime Ministers that we'd have to do it in three.
sentences.zh: 但澳大利亚总理实在太多了，我们得用三集才行。

sentences.en: And we've come now to probably the Australian Prime Minister, who, to the average POM, would be the kind of the platonic ideal of an Australian Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 现在我们讲到了这位澳大利亚总理，对于普通英国人来说，他大概就是澳大利亚总理的柏拉图式理想型。

sentences.en: He's the paradigm of an Australian Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 他是澳大利亚总理的典范。

sentences.en: He's kind of square-jawed, craggy, loves a pint.
sentences.zh: 他下巴方正，轮廓粗犷，热爱喝啤酒。

sentences.en: And in fact, I mean, his great feat, he was a Rhodes Scholar at Oxford.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他最伟大的壮举之一，就是他曾是牛津大学的罗德学者。

sentences.en: He set the world record for downing a yard of ale in 11 seconds.
sentences.zh: 他创下了11秒喝完一码长啤酒杯的世界纪录。

sentences.en: He did it in 11 seconds.
sentences.zh: 他只用了11秒。

sentences.en: So just for people who don't know, which I assume is 99% of people, a yard of ale.
sentences.zh: 给不知道的人解释一下，我猜99%的人都不知道，什么是“一码啤酒”。

sentences.en: It's a very thin, long glass.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常细长的玻璃杯。

sentences.en: And I think they have it at the Turf Tavern in Oxford.
sentences.zh: 我想牛津的草皮酒馆（Turf Tavern）里就有。

sentences.en: Tom, if you've ever been to the Turf, a kind of classic Oxford pub, they have it behind the bar.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，如果你去过草皮酒馆，那是一家经典的牛津酒吧，吧台后面就挂着那个杯子。

sentences.en: And I think that's the yard of ale that Bob Hawke downed.
sentences.zh: 我想那就是鲍勃·霍克喝过的那只一码啤酒杯。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a colossal amount of ale.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那可是海量的啤酒。

sentences.en: Yeah, because it's the photos of him up there, I think, doing it.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为上面还有他当时喝啤酒的照片。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And he downed it in 11 seconds.
sentences.zh: 他用了11秒就喝干了。

sentences.en: And as a feat, I mean, that is unsurpassed.
sentences.zh: 作为一项壮举，这简直是无人能及。

sentences.en: I mean, that was a world record.
sentences.zh: 那可是世界纪录。

sentences.en: I think it still is, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想现在应该还是吧？

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: I'm not sure if it's been beaten.
sentences.zh: 我不确定是否有人打破过。

sentences.en: But anyway, Bob Hawke.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，这就是鲍勃·霍克。

sentences.en: So in our previous podcasts about Australia, certainly in the first one, which was less about trousers and more about genuine kind of themes
sentences.zh: 在我们之前关于澳大利亚的播客中，当然是在第一期，那期不怎么谈裤子，更多是关于澳大利亚政治史的真正主题，

sentences.en: of Australian political history, we talked about the religious stuff, which I know obviously sort of you enjoy.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了宗教方面的内容，我知道你显然对此很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And how many of them, how many Australian, senior Australian politicians came from religious backgrounds or backgrounds in which they had maybe abjured their religion
sentences.zh: 有多少澳大利亚的高层政客出身于宗教背景，或者他们可能已经背弃了宗教，

sentences.en: and there was still a kind of sense of mission and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但心中依然有一种使命感之类的东西。

sentences.en: And that's very true.
sentences.zh: 这非常准确。

sentences.en: I mean, Bob Hawke appears to be this kind of hard-drinking, you know, barbecue-loving Mr. Australia.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·霍克看起来像是那种豪饮、热爱烧烤的“澳大利亚先生”。

sentences.en: But his father was a Congregationalist pastor.
sentences.zh: 但他父亲是一位公理会牧师。

sentences.en: And as a boy, he was brought up in this atmosphere of sort of almost sort of suffocating religious intensity.
sentences.zh: 他小时候是在一种近乎令人窒息的宗教氛围中长大的。

sentences.en: So his father told him, according to his biographer, that he should believe in the fatherhood of God and that heaven was all around him and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 据他的传记作者说，他父亲告诉他，他应该相信上帝的父性，天堂就在他周围，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And he absolutely grows up in that atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是在那种氛围中长大的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it won't surprise you to hear that obviously I think that there's an incredibly Christian strain within the left's approach to policy.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你听到我认为左翼的政策方针中存在一种极其浓厚的基督教色彩，你一定不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, Hawke is essentially, I mean, that's what his politics is, a secularised version of those kind of Christian principles.
sentences.zh: 你知道，霍克本质上就是这样，他的政治主张就是那些基督教原则的世俗化版本。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对正确。

sentences.en: So apparently when he was a boy growing up in,
sentences.zh: 显然，当他还是个孩子的时候，在……

sentences.en: what was he growing up?
sentences.zh: 他在哪里长大的？

sentences.en: He was growing up in a place called Bordertown.
sentences.zh: 他在一个叫博德敦的地方长大。

sentences.en: And he gets a scholarship to school in Perth and so on.
sentences.zh: 后来他拿到了去珀斯上学的奖学金，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But when he's a boy, I mean, these are not sort of glamorous places by Australian standards.
sentences.zh: 但他小时候，按澳大利亚的标准来看，这些地方并不算繁华。

sentences.en: But even when he's a boy, because he's so clever, his family joke and they'll say he'll be prime minister one day.
sentences.zh: 但即使在他小时候，因为他太聪明了，家里人开玩笑说他将来会成为总理。

sentences.en: And he goes off to the University of Western Australia to study law.
sentences.zh: 后来他去西澳大利亚大学学习法律。

sentences.en: And he's riding home on his motorbike when he feels something wrong.
sentences.zh: 有一天他骑摩托车回家时，感觉有些不对劲。

sentences.en: And he has this crash, this terrible crash.
sentences.zh: 然后他遭遇了车祸，一场可怕的车祸。

sentences.en: And he almost is killed.
sentences.zh: 他差点丧命。

sentences.en: He spends days between life and death.
sentences.zh: 他在生死边缘徘徊了几天。

sentences.en: And his mother says to him, you've been spared and it's a sign of God's providence.
sentences.zh: 他母亲对他说，你大难不死，这是上帝眷顾的迹象。

sentences.en: And Hawke absolutely believes it.
sentences.zh: 霍克对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: He says later, he says later, I firmly believe that God had spared my life.
sentences.zh: 他后来多次表示，我坚信是上帝挽救了我的生命。

sentences.en: He thinks he's been given this new chance and he's determined not to waste it.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己获得了新生，并决心不再浪费生命。

sentences.en: And that basically drives him into sort of good works and so on.
sentences.zh: 这基本上促使他投身于慈善事业等等。

sentences.en: It doesn't stop him drinking, does it?
sentences.zh: 但这并没有让他戒酒，对吧？

sentences.en: It doesn't stop him drinking.
sentences.zh: 确实没让他戒酒。

sentences.en: So he literally has alcohol poisoning in 1963.
sentences.zh: 他在1963年甚至还酒精中毒过。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实有过。

sentences.en: But he's also by that point, he's given up his faith because you know why?
sentences.zh: 但到那时他也放弃了信仰，你知道为什么吗？

sentences.en: He went to India with the World Conference of Christian Youth.
sentences.zh: 他参加了世界基督教青年大会，去了印度。

sentences.en: And he was really shocked that the World Conference of Christian Youth were having a great time.
sentences.zh: 他非常震惊，因为世界基督教青年大会的人竟然玩得那么开心。

sentences.en: You know, they're staying in nice places and presumably knowing him getting lashed every night.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们住着高档酒店，以他的性格，估计每晚都在酗酒。

sentences.en: He's struck by the contrast with the poverty of the people around them.
sentences.zh: 他被这种奢靡与周围民众的贫困形成的鲜明对比所震撼。

sentences.en: And he thinks he can't reconcile this.
sentences.zh: 他觉得无法调和这种矛盾。

sentences.en: And he basically loses his faith.
sentences.zh: 于是他基本上失去了信仰。

sentences.en: But as you say, Tom, he retains that sense of mission.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，汤姆，他保留了那种使命感。

sentences.en: That sense of mission, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那种使命感，没错。

sentences.en: But he sort of, that brings him into trade unionism and trade union politics.
sentences.zh: 但这让他投身于工会运动和工会政治。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so we talked, we mentioned him briefly in our discussion of Whitlam,
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在讨论惠特拉姆时简要提到了他，

sentences.en: Goff-Whitlam affair yesterday.
sentences.zh: 昨天讨论的戈夫·惠特拉姆事件。

sentences.en: He was very prominent, trade union leader.
sentences.zh: 他当时非常显眼，是一位工会领袖。

sentences.en: And that provides him with the springboard then to enter politics.
sentences.zh: 这为他进入政坛提供了跳板。

sentences.en: But he's also interesting.
sentences.zh: 但他也很特别。

sentences.en: He's very pro-American.
sentences.zh: 他非常亲美。

sentences.en: Yeah, I saw this.
sentences.zh: 没错，我看到了。

sentences.en: He's actually kind of informant to the US.
sentences.zh: 他实际上算是美国的线人。

sentences.en: So, yeah, kind of, you know, an interesting combination.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，这是一种有趣的组合。

sentences.en: But there is that tradition in Australian politics, as indeed in British politics, of sort of very self-consciously patriotic in Australia, obviously even more so anti-communist,
sentences.zh: 但在澳大利亚政治中确实有这种传统，就像在英国政治中一样，那种非常自觉的爱国主义，在澳大利亚显然更是反共的，

sentences.en: kind of pro-Western alliance, kind of left-wing politics.
sentences.zh: 那种支持西方联盟的左翼政治。

sentences.en: James Callahan.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·卡拉汉。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, James Callahan, Dennis Healy, that kind of, I mean, I think Hawke absolutely kind of conforms to that pattern.
sentences.zh: 没错，詹姆斯·卡拉汉、丹尼斯·希利，那种类型，我认为霍克完全符合这种模式。

sentences.en: It's remarkable that he enters parliament only three years before he becomes prime minister.
sentences.zh: 令人惊叹的是，他在成为总理前仅仅进入议会三年。

sentences.en: Yeah, and fans of Le Carre will be very excited to learn the name of the Labour leader who he replaces, which is Bill Hayden.
sentences.zh: 没错，勒卡雷的粉丝们如果知道他取代的工党领袖的名字是比尔·海登，一定会非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Oh, I went, I went.
sentences.zh: 哦，我去了，我去了。

sentences.en: No, we shouldn't give it away.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不应该剧透。

sentences.en: But Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy.
sentences.zh: 但《锅匠，裁缝，士兵，间谍》……

sentences.en: Yeah, it's great that he does replace him.
sentences.zh: 没错，他取代了那个人，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Hawke is an incredibly successful prime minister.
sentences.zh: 霍克是一位极其成功的总理。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, interestingly, so, as you say, he's got this kind of, you know, this image of being the plain-speaking, craggy.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，正如你所说，他给人留下的印象是直言不讳、性格粗犷。

sentences.en: I mean, he is, he really is a man's man, isn't he, with all this, these drinking feats, even though he's given up booze.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他确实是个纯爷们，不是吗？尽管他戒了酒，但他有那么多喝酒的壮举。

sentences.en: Yeah, he gives it up.
sentences.zh: 没错，他戒了。

sentences.en: He pledges to give it up when he enters parliament and he sticks to that.
sentences.zh: 他进入议会时发誓戒酒，并且坚持了下来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Until he leaves office.
sentences.zh: 直到他卸任。

sentences.en: But his politics are a really interesting mix because he basically revives and intensifies the universal healthcare that Gough Whitlam had tried to pioneer
sentences.zh: 但他的政治主张是一种非常有趣的混合体，因为他基本上恢复并加强了戈夫·惠特拉姆在70年代试图开创的全民医疗保健体系，

sentences.en: in the 70s, but also in his economic stuff.
sentences.zh: 但在经济政策上也是如此。

sentences.en: That, I mean, that, that looks all very reforming and stuff, but it's actually not that dissimilar from what the Batra government is doing in Britain.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是非常激进的改革，但实际上与撒切尔政府在英国所做的事情并无太大不同。

sentences.en: And so floating the Australian dollar, deregulating the economy, bringing down tariffs,
sentences.zh: 比如让澳元浮动、放松经济管制、降低关税、

sentences.en: bringing down barriers, all that sort of stuff, basically opening the Australian economy up to globalisation and to the economic trends of the late 20th century.
sentences.zh: 打破壁垒等等，基本上是向全球化和20世纪末的经济趋势开放澳大利亚经济。

sentences.en: You know, he's doing it from a left-wing sort of perspective,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是从左翼的角度来做这件事的，

sentences.en: but it's not really that dissimilar from what Thatcher and Geoffrey Howe were doing in Britain from a right-wing standpoint in the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 但这与撒切尔和杰弗里·豪在80年代初从右翼立场在英国所做的事情并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: And it's, and it's funny that the people so rarely draw parallels between the two because you're so imprisoned by kind of partisanship.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，人们很少将两者进行比较，因为你们被党派偏见所束缚。

sentences.en: Well, I think also because the example of Hawke and then Keating, who succeeds him, are so influential on new Labour in Britain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为也是因为霍克以及继任者基廷的例子，对英国的新工党影响太深了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 没错，我认为这绝对正确。

sentences.en: But you, yeah, I mean, it's, it's, it's, it's a fascinating parallel, really is.
sentences.zh: 但你……没错，这确实是一个引人入胜的平行案例。

sentences.en: But you mentioned Keating, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但你提到了基廷，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a great partnership, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是一对伟大的搭档，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's one of the, that's the, arguably the great partnership.
sentences.zh: 那是……可以说是一对伟大的搭档。

sentences.en: Well, it's the partnership that goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是最终分道扬镳的搭档。

sentences.en: So again, a bit like, I mean, I'm sorry for Australian listeners to endlessly reducing it to parallels with new Labour, but there's a kind of Blair Brown dynamic going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次重申，我很抱歉让澳大利亚听众不断地将其与新工党进行类比，但那里确实存在一种布莱尔与布朗式的动态关系。

sentences.en: So the interesting thing about Hawke is that he, as you say, was a Rhodes scholar.
sentences.zh: 关于霍克，有趣的一点是，正如你所说，他曾是罗德学者。

sentences.en: He didn't really like Oxford and didn't like the British, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他并不真正喜欢牛津，也不喜欢英国人。

sentences.en: No, and so he, he legislates to remove, you know, the last kind of links to.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以他立法废除了与英国的最后联系。

sentences.en: Well, he gets rid of the anthem, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他废除了国歌，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The, he says at one point, it's absolutely ridiculous that basically when the British win some, win an Olympic gold, they get up and it's God save the Queen.
sentences.zh: 他曾说，当英国人赢得奥运金牌时，大家起立奏响《天佑女王》，这简直太荒谬了。

sentences.en: If we beat them, it's also God save the Queen.
sentences.zh: 如果我们打败了他们，奏的还是《天佑女王》。

sentences.en: Which I think is, is probably fair enough.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这话说得挺有道理的。

sentences.en: But, but I think partly because he's a Rhodes scholar and he's so clever and he's so successful and all of this stuff, he can play the part very happily of the ordinary guy.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，部分因为他是罗德学者，极其聪明且成就斐然，他可以非常自如地扮演普通人的角色。

sentences.en: Cause he doesn't, he's got nothing to lose, you know?
sentences.zh: 因为他没什么可失去的，你懂吗？

sentences.en: So he doesn't have any psychological hangups about people thinking he's stupid or anything.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有任何心理负担，不用担心别人觉得他愚蠢之类的。

sentences.en: So he can sort of say, well, all I'm interested in is gambling, watching loads of sports, smoking cigars, um, obviously would have been alcohol in the old days.

sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.zh: 军情五处。

sentences.en: Who published a book called Spycatcher, which he'll know all about, Dominic, because it's all about Harold Wilson.
sentences.zh: 他出版了一本叫《捕谍者》的书，多米尼克，他对此应该很了解，因为书里全是关于哈罗德·威尔逊的内容。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He claimed that he and lots of other MI5 agents had conspired against Harold Wilson when Harold
sentences.zh: 他声称他和许多其他军情五处特工曾密谋反对哈罗德·威尔逊，当时哈罗德

sentences.en: Wilson was prime minister of Britain in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊是20世纪70年代的英国首相。

sentences.en: And so Mr. Thatcher brought in the Official Secrets Act, didn't she?
sentences.zh: 所以撒切尔夫人引入了《官方机密法》，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的，为了试图……并且说，你们不能出版它。

sentences.en: And so he published it in Australia.
sentences.zh: 于是他在澳大利亚出版了。

sentences.en: And so the full might of the British civil service, kind of the most elegant yes minister type mandarins went over there and were humiliated by Turnbull.
sentences.zh: 结果英国公务员系统的全部力量，那些最优雅的“是，大臣”式的官僚们去了那里，却被特恩布尔羞辱了。

sentences.en: Is it economical with the truth?
sentences.zh: 是“对真相轻描淡写”吗？

sentences.en: I think Robert Armstrong, who was head of the British civil service, was kind of admitted basically to having lied.
sentences.zh: 我想罗伯特·阿姆斯特朗，那位英国公务员系统的负责人，基本上算是承认自己撒了谎。

sentences.en: So it was all a disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以那简直是一场灾难。

sentences.en: And on top of that, Turnbull was a very prominent Republican.
sentences.zh: 而且最重要的是，特恩布尔是一位非常著名的共和派人士。

sentences.en: Which is interesting, given that he's on the right of Australian politics.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他属于澳大利亚右翼政治阵营，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's why he could easily have been Labour.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么他本可以轻易加入工党。

sentences.en: Because he was the chair, wasn't he, of the campaign for a Republican, because they had a referendum in 1999.
sentences.zh: 因为他是共和运动的主席，对吧？因为他们在1999年举行了公投。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So yes, he's very much on the sort of, the softer wing, I suppose, of the Australian right.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我认为他非常属于澳大利亚右翼中比较温和的那一派。

sentences.en: But, surprise, surprise, he doesn't sit easily on the throne for long, does he?
sentences.zh: 但是，令人惊讶的是，他并没有在那个位置上坐得太久，不是吗？

sentences.en: What has he got?
sentences.zh: 他干了多久？

sentences.en: Three years?
sentences.zh: 三年？

sentences.en: And then he's knifed by the abbots, the abbotists?
sentences.zh: 然后就被阿博特派，那些阿博特主义者给捅了？

sentences.en: What were the abbotists?
sentences.zh: 什么是阿博特主义者？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Were they called the abbotists?
sentences.zh: 他们真的叫阿博特主义者吗？

sentences.en: I suppose, yes.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: The abbotards.
sentences.zh: 阿博特党徒。

sentences.en: The mad monks.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的僧侣们。

sentences.en: And he was succeeded by Scott Morrison.
sentences.zh: 接替他的是斯科特·莫里森。

sentences.en: Now, Scott Morrison has, of course, as our listeners will now know-
sentences.zh: 现在，斯科特·莫里森，当然，正如我们的听众现在所知道的——

sentences.en: May no longer be prime minister.
sentences.zh: 可能已经不再是总理了。

sentences.en: There were no Scott Morrison's feet.
sentences.zh: 斯科特·莫里森的脚印已经不在了。

sentences.en: By the time you listen to this.
sentences.zh: 当你听到这段话时。

sentences.en: And I have to say, of Scott Morrison, to me, he just looks like a man at a garden centre.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，对于斯科特·莫里森，在我看来，他看起来就像个在园艺中心的人。

sentences.en: I don't really have anything to say about him.
sentences.zh: 关于他我实在没什么可说的。

sentences.en: He looks like a koala.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像只考拉。

sentences.en: Do you think so?
sentences.zh: 你也这么觉得吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He knocked somebody over.
sentences.zh: 他撞倒了某个人。

sentences.en: He knocked a child over.
sentences.zh: 他撞倒了一个孩子。

sentences.en: He was playing football.
sentences.zh: 他当时在踢足球。

sentences.en: He was playing football.
sentences.zh: 他当时在踢足球。

sentences.en: He did a Boris Johnson, basically.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是搞了一次“鲍里斯·约翰逊式”的表演。

sentences.en: And also, that was very funny.
sentences.zh: 而且那件事非常滑稽。

sentences.en: He was out campaigning and giving a speech on a lawn.
sentences.zh: 他当时在外面竞选，正在草坪上发表演讲。

sentences.en: And the bloke whose lawn it was came out and said, get off my lawn.
sentences.zh: 结果那块草坪的主人走出来说，从我的草坪上滚开。

sentences.en: Yes, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是真的。

sentences.en: So that was fun.
sentences.zh: 所以那很有趣。

sentences.en: That was very nicely sort of egalitarian Australian, I thought.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那非常具有澳大利亚式的平等主义色彩。

sentences.en: He did just get off the lawn.
sentences.zh: 他确实就从草坪上走开了。

sentences.en: He was like, oh, sorry.
sentences.zh: 他当时就像是，哦，抱歉。

sentences.en: And he got off the lawn.
sentences.zh: 然后他就离开了草坪。

sentences.en: But he seems the kind of man to whom these things happen.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎就是那种会发生这类事情的人。

sentences.en: Slightly gaffed prone.
sentences.zh: 稍微有点容易出洋相。

sentences.en: So his big gaff was that in 2019-20, that summer in Australia, there were terrible, terrible bushfires.
sentences.zh: 他最大的失态是在2019-20年，那个夏天在澳大利亚发生了极其可怕的森林大火。

sentences.en: And you remember talking of koalas.
sentences.zh: 说到考拉，你还记得吗。

sentences.en: All the koalas burnt to death.
sentences.zh: 所有的考拉都被烧死了。

sentences.en: It was absolutely awful.
sentences.zh: 那真是太可怕了。

sentences.en: Kind of the highest temperatures Australia had ever known.
sentences.zh: 那是澳大利亚有史以来最高的温度。

sentences.en: And he was on holiday in Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 而他当时正在夏威夷度假。

sentences.en: Oh, that's right.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This did not go down well.
sentences.zh: 这事儿反响很不好。

sentences.en: And the other thing, I guess, for which he's recently been...
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事，我想，他最近被……

sentences.en: I mean, he had a good COVID, I think.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得他在新冠疫情期间表现不错。

sentences.en: I mean, he managed it quite well.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他处理得相当好。

sentences.en: He maintained fortress Australia and then brought the vaccine in.
sentences.zh: 他维持了“堡垒澳大利亚”，然后引进了疫苗。

sentences.en: So Australia's death rate's been much lower than it was in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以澳大利亚的死亡率比欧洲要低得多。

sentences.en: But he...
sentences.zh: 但他……

sentences.en: Oh, and AUKUS, you said the submarine deal.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有AUKUS，你提到的潜艇协议。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: He annoyed the French.
sentences.zh: 他惹恼了法国人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he kind of presided over the Djokovic debacle.
sentences.zh: 但他基本上主持了德约科维奇那场闹剧。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Was it a debacle?
sentences.zh: 那是一场闹剧吗？

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: Well, I think he was trying to leverage it because he had the election coming up and he thought it would play well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他当时试图利用这件事，因为选举临近，他觉得这会对他有利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it all got scrambled with kind of government, you know, federal and state levels.
sentences.zh: 但事情在政府层面，你知道，联邦和州级别，全都搞乱了。

sentences.en: So anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: And also he's a PentecostaliSt.
sentences.zh: 而且他还是个五旬节派教徒。

sentences.en: Is he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Does he speak in tongues?
sentences.zh: 他会说方言吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if he does.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他会不会。

sentences.en: I mean, I think he kind of periodically in interviews, he's intimated that he does.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得他在采访中偶尔暗示过他会。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: But he's never done it in an interview.
sentences.zh: 但他从未在采访中展示过。

sentences.en: So he...
sentences.zh: 所以他……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He does think that trolls on social media are literally emanations of the devil.
sentences.zh: 他确实认为社交媒体上的喷子是魔鬼的化身。

sentences.en: Well, that will be a relief to you, Tom, when you get abused from academics on...
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，当你受到学术界人士的辱骂时，这会让你感到宽慰的……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Satan is speaking.
sentences.zh: 那是撒旦在说话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we'll see.
sentences.zh: 所以我们走着瞧吧。

sentences.en: So the question is, I mean, obviously, that culture of spills is ridiculous and probably very damaging to good government because it just means, you know, prime ministers have
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，我是说，显然，那种频繁更换领导人的文化是荒谬的，而且可能对良好的政府治理非常有害，因为它意味着，你知道，总理们

sentences.en: come and go within two years and presumably spent an enormous amount of time watching their backs.
sentences.zh: 在两年内来来去去，想必花了大量时间提防背后捅刀子。

sentences.en: Do you think...
sentences.zh: 你认为……

sentences.en: I mean, we talked about some of these Robert Menzies and, you know, Bob Hawke and so on,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们谈到了一些像罗伯特·孟席斯，还有，鲍勃·霍克等等，

sentences.en: Gough Whitlam.
sentences.zh: 高夫·惠特拉姆。

sentences.en: Do you think it's fair to say that the standard has declined?
sentences.zh: 你认为说水平下降了公平吗？

sentences.en: I don't know enough about Australian politics to say that.
sentences.zh: 我对澳大利亚政治了解不够，无法评价。

sentences.en: But my feeling is that we always think that the politicians who are around more recent are less effective.
sentences.zh: 但我的感觉是，我们总是认为最近出现的政治家效率较低。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然会这么想。

sentences.en: Of course we do.
sentences.zh: 我们当然会。

sentences.en: Because we always kind of, you know, already we're looking back and saying, oh, you know, remember the golden days of Theresa May and Jeremy Corbyn, what giants they were.
sentences.zh: 因为我们总是，你知道，已经在回顾过去并说，哦，你知道，记得特蕾莎·梅和杰里米·科尔宾的黄金时代吗，他们是多么伟大的巨人。

sentences.en: Well, I think, I mean, because people often say this about British politics, which has also been very unstable in the last 10 years or so at the top.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，我是说，因为人们经常这样评价英国政治，过去十年左右，英国政治在顶层也非常不稳定。

sentences.en: And the one thing that occurs to me is just, I mean, it's true.
sentences.zh: 我想到的一点是，我是说，这是真的。

sentences.en: People have always said the standards were falling.
sentences.zh: 人们一直说标准在下降。

sentences.en: I mean, there's never a point where people didn't bemoan the collapse in political leadership.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从来没有哪个时候人们不哀叹政治领导力的崩溃。

sentences.en: But the fact that people always say it doesn't therefore mean...
sentences.zh: 但人们总是这么说，并不意味着……

sentences.en: Meaning it's not true.
sentences.zh: 意味着这不是真的。

sentences.en: That it's not true, that it can never fall.
sentences.zh: 意味着它不是真的，意味着它永远不会下降。

sentences.en: I mean, I think Kevin Rudd, Julia Gillard, Malcolm Turnbull, Scott Morrison, Tony Abbott, are they of the same stature as the prime ministers?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为凯文·陆克文、朱莉娅·吉拉德、马尔科姆·特恩布尔、斯科特·莫里森、托尼·阿博特，他们和那些总理们是同一个量级的吗？

sentences.en: Are they genuinely of the same stature as the prime ministers of the 1940s and 1950s?
sentences.zh: 他们真的和20世纪40年代和50年代的总理们是同一个量级的吗？

sentences.en: Or are we only saying that because the context is different, because we're less deferential?
sentences.zh: 还是我们只是因为背景不同，因为我们不再那么恭顺，才这么说的？

sentences.en: You know, these are difficult questions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些都是难题。

sentences.en: I think Hawke and Keating were clearly exceptional politicians, but also exceptional...
sentences.zh: 我认为霍克和基廷显然是杰出的政治家，但也是杰出的……

sentences.en: They weren't just politicians.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是政治家。

sentences.en: They were masters of the art of politics, but they put it to purposes that were very influential, not just within the context of Australian politics, but internationally.
sentences.zh: 他们是政治艺术的大师，但他们将其用于非常有影响力的目的，不仅是在澳大利亚政治背景下，而且在国际上也是如此。

sentences.en: So in a sense, they blazed the path for Clinton and Blair and Schroeder and all that kind of tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，他们为克林顿、布莱尔、施罗德以及所有那种传统开辟了道路。

sentences.en: And I think that since then, Australia's circumstances, because it has all these mineral resources
sentences.zh: 我认为从那时起，澳大利亚的情况，因为它拥有所有这些矿产资源

sentences.en: and it has this relationship with China, has meant that it's slightly uncoupled itself from trends within, say, Europe or America.
sentences.zh: 并且与中国有这种关系，意味着它已经稍微脱离了比如欧洲或美国的趋势。

sentences.en: But I think that that relationship with China, which has been an issue in Australian politics right from the point of federation, is becoming more unstable again,
sentences.zh: 但我认为与中国的这种关系，从联邦成立之初就是澳大利亚政治的一个议题，现在又变得更加不稳定了。

sentences.en: which is why Scott Morrison signed that...
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么斯科特·莫里森签署了那个……

sentences.en: The AUKUS.
sentences.zh: 奥库斯协议。

sentences.en: They've been, yeah, the AUKUS deal.
sentences.zh: 他们一直，没错，就是奥库斯协议。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, we don't know, obviously, the results of the Australian election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然我们还不知道澳大利亚大选的结果。

sentences.en: When we did our first podcast, we thought it would be coming out in the wake of the Australian.
sentences.zh: 当我们制作第一期播客时，我们以为它会在澳大利亚大选结束后发布。

sentences.en: I mean, there may have been several prime ministers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，可能已经换了好几任总理了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the first one, this will be, what, four or five days after the elections?
sentences.zh: 所以第一期，这大概是选举结束后的四五天吧？

sentences.en: So who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Given their enthusiasm for stabbing each other in the back.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们热衷于背后捅刀子。

sentences.en: But I suppose the real, for me, the real revelation of this is just how incredibly interesting Australian politics is.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对我来说，这其中真正的启示是澳大利亚政治竟然如此引人入胜。

sentences.en: And the irony that in Britain, we are so ignorant of it and we think of it as just unbelievably boring.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，在英国，我们对它知之甚少，还觉得它无聊透顶。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I think it's a tribute.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种致敬。

sentences.en: But I think it has been quite influential.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它确实很有影响力。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, we talked, Tony Abbott's immigration policies have been influential on conservatives here.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，我们谈到过，托尼·阿博特的移民政策对这里的保守派产生了影响。

sentences.en: Where the Hawke-Keating governments were very, very influential on Blair and Brown.
sentences.zh: 霍克-基廷政府对布莱尔和布朗的影响也非常非常大。

sentences.en: So I think that, you know, absolutely, politicians certainly are alert to Australia.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，绝对是这样，政客们当然对澳大利亚保持着警觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Jolly good.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, thank you very much for bearing with us for three episodes of what was meant to be a short gallop.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家包容我们，原本计划短小精悍的系列竟然做了三期。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, Dominic, when we began this podcast, would you have thought we'd do three episodes or not?
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，当我们开始这个播客时，你想到我们会做三期吗？

sentences.en: I didn't.
sentences.zh: 我没想过。

sentences.en: But, I mean, that was several days ago.
sentences.zh: 但那已经是几天前的事了。

sentences.zh: 那么，音乐先生，请再吹奏一次你的迪吉里杜管，为我们送行好吗？

sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 再见。
